title: Protein Language Models Identify Early Folding Residues as Critical Hotspots for Pathogenic Variants and Cancer Prognosis.
authors: Guo, Lisha; Yuan, Fuchong; Zhou, Na; Zhao, Minghui; Liu, Ruotong; Jing, Ming; Feenstra, K Anton; Hou, Qingzhen
one_liner_zh: 该文开发了基于蛋白语言模型的LMEFold框架，从序列预测早期折叠残基，并揭示其与致病突变和癌症预后的关联，核心贡献在蛋白质结构相关计算建模，方法创新且应用广泛。
abstract: Identifying the specific residues that initiate protein folding is critical for understanding protein stability and the mechanisms of misfolding-related diseases. However, the systematic, proteome-wide identification of these early folding residues (EFRs) has been hampered by both experimental and computational limitations. Here, we present LMEFold, a deep learning framework using protein language models (PLMs) to accurately predict EFRs from amino acid sequence alone. LMEFold outperforms existing sequence-based predictors on the Start2Fold benchmark (ROC AUC = 0.831), and its predicted scores show consistent associations with independent HDX-NMR protection-factor measurements, providing complementary biophysical evidence. Applying LMEFold to annotate over 6.6 million variants across diverse genomic datasets, we find that pathogenic mutations curated in ClinVar are significantly enriched within EFRs (~17%) compared to millions of population variants from large-scale cohorts including the UKB and gnomAD databases (~10%, P < 0.001). Critically, in the MSK-MET pan-cancer clinical cohort, EFR mutations are associated with severe functional disruption and significantly reduced overall patient survival. Structural analysis of hotspot cancer mutations, such as TP53 p.Y163C, suggests a mechanism whereby these variants destabilize protein structure by disrupting the early folding core. Our work establishes EFRs as critical sites of pathogenic vulnerability and provides a powerful framework for the rapid identification of folding-centric prognostic markers using sequence only.
abstract_zh: 识别启动蛋白质折叠的特异性残基对于理解蛋白质稳定性及错误折叠相关疾病的机制至关重要。然而，系统性地、全蛋白质组范围内鉴定这些早期折叠残基（EFRs）一直受到实验和计算限制的阻碍。在此，我们提出LMEFold，一种利用蛋白质语言模型（PLMs）的深度学习框架，仅从氨基酸序列即可准确预测EFRs。LMEFold在Start2Fold基准测试上优于现有基于序列的预测器（ROC AUC = 0.831），其预测得分与独立的HDX-NMR保护因子测量结果表现出一致关联，提供了互补的生物物理学证据。将LMEFold应用于跨多个基因组数据集的超过660万个变异注释，我们发现ClinVar中整理的致病突变在EFRs内显著富集（约17%），而来自大规模队列（包括UKB和gnomAD数据库）的数百万群体变异中这一比例约为10%（P < 0.001）。关键的是，在MSK-MET泛癌临床队列中，EFR突变与严重功能破坏及患者总生存期显著缩短相关。对热点癌症突变（如TP53 p.Y163C）的结构分析提示，这些变异通过破坏早期折叠核心来使蛋白质结构不稳定。我们的工作确立了EFRs作为致病脆弱性的关键位点，并提供了一种仅利用序列快速识别以折叠为中心的预后标志物的强大框架。
